comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C22-C24, C29, C31-C32, C67) about Ca²⁺-VSD coupling and voltage shifts. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong experimental measurements, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN due to concerns about the magnitude discrepancy with Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) and insufficient explanation of methodological differences.

Both address kinetic analysis claims (C25-C28). OpenEval finds the temporal separation between gating current and channel opening SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN and request additional ionic current comparisons at the same voltages, particularly at high Ca²⁺, to ensure QC is not contaminated by channel opening.

Both evaluate Ca²⁺ dose-response effects on gating currents (C33-C38). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, questioning how small kinetic changes can be reconciled with the proposed 26-fold equilibrium constant change and requesting more complete kinetic characterization.

Both assess model comparison claims (C40-C53, C96). OpenEval finds the statistical evidence SUPPORTED and favoring Scheme II, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting that both models use only one Ca²⁺ site per subunit (inconsistent with Figure 4 findings) and that neither model fits the data well. Reviewers request testing with two Ca²⁺ binding sites per subunit.

Both evaluate claims about equal contributions from RCK1 and RCK2 sites (C55-C66, C86-C87). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers describing the evidence as 'compelling' that both sites independently and additively influence VSD equilibrium.

Both address the discrepancy with Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) (C68-C70). Both rate this UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the discrepancy is not resolved and creates uncertainty about generalizability. Peer reviewers strongly critique the handling, stating it's insufficient to claim the issue is resolved by replicating earlier results from the same lab, and request rigorous assessment of potential reasons for differences.

Both discuss fluorescence studies and CTD-VSD coupling (C71-C75 overlap). OpenEval finds the cited prior work SUPPORTED as providing orthogonal evidence. Peer reviewers also find these background claims SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting them as established context for interpreting current findings.

Partial overlap on structural interpretations (C76, C78-C80). OpenEval rates mechanistic model claims UNCERTAIN due to speculation and contradictions with prior literature. Peer reviewers find structural basis SUPPORTED from cryo-EM studies but note that mechanistic details (e.g., C-linker pulling vs. non-covalent interactions) remain open and current data insufficient to exclude alternative mechanisms.

Both evaluate cooperativity between Ca²⁺ sites (C88-C95). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN due to conflicting evidence and inability to resolve the issue definitively. Peer reviewers rate it SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation as consistent with data and appropriately cautious in discussing potential cooperativity.

Both address established background on BK channel structure and function (C1-C9, C13-C17 overlap). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find these claims SUPPORTED as well-established foundational knowledge with appropriate citations to published literature.

Both evaluate methods claims (C97-C107). OpenEval finds the methods SUPPORTED as appropriate and standard. Peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, not directly challenging the methods but requesting substantial additional methodological details, clarification of grounding scheme, and objective comparison with Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) methodology to explain discrepancies.

Minor overlap on kinetic claims (C30). OpenEval finds kinetic analysis SUPPORTED in R2. Peer R6 questions reconciliation of small kinetic changes with large equilibrium constant changes, rating UNCERTAIN and requesting more complete OFF kinetics data.

Minor overlap on charge recovery observation (C39). OpenEval includes this in SUPPORTED dose-response analysis (R3). Peer reviewers accept this as experimental data without challenge (R11, SUPPORTED), supporting reversibility of voltage sensor movement.
Overlap on mutagenesis background (C54, C56, C59-C60, C85). Both find these SUPPORTED as well-established structural and functional assignments from cited literature without challenge.

Overlap on prior literature suggesting RCK1 dominance (C82-C84). OpenEval notes this contradicts current findings of equal contributions, rating mechanistic model UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers accept these as established background (SUPPORTED) providing context.

Minor overlap on mutagenesis evidence (C81). OpenEval includes this in UNCERTAIN mechanistic synthesis (R8). Peer reviewers accept this specific claim as SUPPORTED based on cited studies, providing evidence for RCK1-VSD coupling.

Minor overlap on general mechanistic framework (C12). OpenEval includes this in SUPPORTED background claims (R10). Peer reviewers also find this conceptual model SUPPORTED by multiple studies, though specific mechanistic details remain unresolved.
